newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends lower but techs gain in cautious session.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends lower but techs gain in cautious session.

text.p: The Dow industrials edged to a modest loss on Wednesday, as investors resumed their cautious ways a day after propelling blue chips to one of their strongest rallies in history.
Technology stocks turned in a solid performance, however, led by sharp rallies in industry leaders like International Business Machines Corp, Intel Corp and Microsoft Corp.
The Dow fell 21 points to close unofficially at 6813.
Earnings reports again dominated the session, with the large cap tech rally in particular linked to anticipation over IBM's first quarter numbers, which were released minutes after the close.
IBM, which rose 2-3/8 to 142-3/8 to lead all Dow gainers on the day, did not disappoint with its earnings of $2.37 per share that matched the very highest of Wall Street estimates.
Intel jumped five points to 146-1/8 and Microsoft rallied 4-1/2 to 115-1/8. But once again, investor caution kept buying interest largely contained to the biggest, best-known names.

"We're not setting the world on fire," said Dick Stein, vice president at U.S. Clearing Corp. "It's a nervous kind of market and when people do come back in, they want to be in high-grade, liquid issues."
As has often been the case during the Dow's recent run, market breadth was fairly weak, with declining issues outnumbering advancers on all the major U.S. exchanges.
Analysts said the narrow buying indicated investors continue to hold broad reservations about some basic fundamentals facing the market, particularly interest rates.
Interest rates pressed higher on the day, as a weak bond market drove yields on the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury up four basis to 7.08 percent in late afternoon.
Analysts said that once the flow of earnings reports ebbs, rate worries would likely once again grip the market.
"Next week, when the focus shifts from earnings, I think the market is going to go down," said David Shulman, chief equity strategist at Salomon Brothers.
Shulman said he expected rates would soon be headed even higher, with a long bond yield rising to 7.5 percent. "That's not going to be friendly for stocks," he said.

Until then, however, earnings remain the dominant theme. Strong quarterly results from US Airways Group Inc propelled that company to a 5-1/4 point surge to 34-1/8, leading a broad advance in transportation stocks.
American Airlines parent company AMR Corp rose three to 91-7/8 and Delta Air Lines Inc added 2-3/4 to finish at 98-1/8.
Reader's Digest Association Inc slumped 2-3/8 to 23-5/8 after that company reported weak third quarter results.
VeriFone Inc jumped 17-1/8 to 47-1/4 after agreeing to be acquired by Hewlett-Packard Co.
Hewlett-Packard, which will swap one share for each of VeriFone's shares, fell 1-1/8 to 49-3/8.
The S&P 500 index fell 0.97 points to 773.64.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 14.40 points to 1227.14.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
